findings.source_passage: whether it was a reality or a dream, I never could entirely settle… it was only two o'clock in the afternoon of the 21st June, the longest day in the year in our hemisphere
findings.why_it_matters: The specific date — 21st June — and 'in our hemisphere' are precise comic/narrative details Melville uses to ground an otherwise dreamlike memory in absurd specificity; cutting them flattens the voice-establishing irony of the passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'two o'clock in the afternoon of the 21st June, the longest day in the year in our hemisphere' verbatim; the specificity is the joke.

findings.source_passage: I went to my little room in the third floor, undressed myself as slowly as possible so as to kill time, and with a bitter sigh got between the sheets.
findings.source_locator: second paragraph, after being sent to bed
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence, with its bathetic precision ('as slowly as possible so as to kill time') and 'a bitter sigh,' is pure Ishmael voice — sardonic, self-dramatizing — and the entire middle of the childhood punishment sequence is excised, removing the build-up that makes the supernatural hand moment earn its weight.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the undressing-slowly and bitter-sigh sentence, and the subsequent paragraph about 'sixteen entire hours' and going to beg his stepmother for a slippering.

findings.source_passage: suddenly threw myself at her feet, beseeching her as a particular favour to give me a good slippering for my misbehaviour; anything indeed but condemning me to lie abed such an unendurable length of time
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most distinctively comic and voice-defining moments in the chapter — Ishmael's mock-heroic self-abasement, preferring a beating to boredom — and it is entirely cut. Critical tradition cites this passage to establish Ishmael's ironic relationship to suffering and his comedic register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the paragraph beginning 'at last I got up, dressed, and softly going down in my stockinged feet' through 'back I had to go to my room' verbatim or near-verbatim; this is non-negotiable voice material.

findings.source_passage: for days and weeks and months afterwards I lost myself in confounding attempts to explain the mystery. Nay, to this very hour, I often puzzle myself with it.
findings.source_locator: third paragraph, closing the supernatural hand memory
findings.why_it_matters: The draft retains only 'Nay, to this very hour, I often puzzle myself with it' but drops 'for days and weeks and months afterwards I lost myself in confounding attempts to explain the mystery,' which is the interpretive bridge establishing the hand as a lasting psychic wound, not mere anecdote.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence about 'days and weeks and months' before the 'Nay' sentence.

findings.source_passage: unlock his bridegroom clasp—yet, sleeping as he was, he still hugged me tightly, as though naught but death should part us twain
findings.source_locator: fourth paragraph, Ishmael trying to free himself
findings.why_it_matters: The 'bridegroom clasp' and 'naught but death should part us twain' are the chapter's marriage-parody motif in concentrated form — critically significant for the homoerotic/companionate reading of Ishmael and Queequeg — and are entirely absent from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'unlock his bridegroom clasp—yet, sleeping as he was, he still hugged me tightly, as though naught but death should part us twain' verbatim; it is interpretively load-bearing.

findings.source_passage: A pretty pickle, truly, thought I; abed here in a strange house in the broad day, with a cannibal and a tomahawk! 'Queequeg!—in the name of goodness, Queequeg, wake!'
findings.source_locator: fourth paragraph, after discovering the tomahawk
findings.why_it_matters: The exclamatory 'A pretty pickle, truly' and the direct comic alarm of the dialogue are signature Ishmael — the ironic understatement followed by mock-panic — and their removal flattens the humor of the scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'A pretty pickle, truly, thought I; abed here in a strange house in the broad day, with a cannibal and a tomahawk!' and the accompanying dialogue.

findings.source_passage: neither caterpillar nor butterfly… He was just enough civilized to show off his outlandishness in the strangest possible manners.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft omits the 'neither caterpillar nor butterfly' formulation, which is the memorable image crystallizing Queequeg's transitional status; the surrounding sentence is retained but loses its punch without the metaphor.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'neither caterpillar nor butterfly' in the 'transition stage' sentence.

summary: The draft excises the entire stepmother-slippering sequence (high-severity signature loss), removes 'bridegroom clasp / naught but death should part us twain' (medium, interpretively critical for the marriage motif), drops 'A pretty pickle' and the alarm dialogue, and truncates several other voice-defining passages, constituting one high and multiple medium failures that require regeneration.
